title: Execution path deviation analysis and quarantine playbook
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Summary: On 2025-02-27 we observed a sustained p95/p99 latency regression across short-sequence text-generation workloads (1-16 tokens). The regression correlated with a canary of runtime-1.22 that included two changes: a scheduler heuristic weight adjustment (reduce queue-wait sensitivity) and a new attention autotiler that exposes a fused quantized kernel. The combination caused the kernel selector to favor a fused quantized path that performs poorly at short lengths on A100 and A10x GPUs, leading to queueing, increased tail latency, and downstream autoscaler oscillation. Impacted customers experienced elevated response times, timeout errors, and transient Dedicated capacity breaches. This ticket tracks the technical analysis, immediate mitigations, and a quarantine + testplaybook to prevent recurrence.

root_cause: Primary cause: combined interaction between a scheduler heuristic parameter change and a profiling-format change consumed by the kernel cost estimator. The estimator misinterpreted microbenchmark samples for fused quantized kernels, underestimating their per-token latency for very short sequences. The scheduler heuristic favored lower-queue-score paths and therefore routed more traffic to the fused quantized kernel, which, for short sequences and certain batch shapes, has higher constant overhead that dominates token-level latency. Secondary cause: lack of guardrails in the kernel selection logic for short-sequence regimes and insufficient synthetic benchmarks covering 1-8 token tails across all supported GPUs.
mitigation_summary: Immediate actions taken: rolled back scheduler heuristic weight, reduced canary percentage, disabled runtime probing for the fused quantized kernel in production, and adjusted autoscaler smoothing to avoid oscillation. Short-term: introduced a runtime quarantine flag to opt-out specific kernels from selection (runtime-quarantine:kq-fused-quant-v4), added a synthetic microbench for 1-16 token shapes to CI and perf jobs, and added targeted dashboards for kernel selection entropy and per-sequence-length p95. Medium-term: update cost estimator to use calibrated latency models per GPU+quantization combination, add a deterministic fallback selector for short sequences, and incorporate query-shape-aware unit tests into premerge checks.
